fasting.title: Fasting Seasons
fasting.p: Fasting is a central part of Ethiopian Orthodox spiritual life. The faithful abstain from all animal products during fasting periods. Major fasting seasons include:

items.name: Hudadi / Lent (Abiy Tsom)
items.description: The Great Fast — the longest and most important fasting period

items.name: Fast of the Apostles (Tsome Hawariat)
items.description: Commemorating the apostles' fasting after receiving the Holy Spirit

items.name: Advent Fast (Tsome Gena)
items.description: Preparation for the birth of Christ (Genna, January 7)

fasting.weekly: Additionally, every Wednesday and Friday are fasting days throughout the year.

feasts.title: Feast of Saint Gabriel & Church Calendar

stGabriel.title: Feast of Archangel Saint Gabriel
stGabriel.p1: As a church named after the Archangel Gabriel, the Feast of Saint Gabriel holds special significance for our community. We celebrate this feast with particular devotion, gathering for extended services, prayer, and fellowship.
stGabriel.p2: The Ark of Archangel Saint Gabriel is found at the renowned Kulubi Saint Gabriel Church, located 462 kilometres from Addis Ababa near Dire Dawa. The church was built by Prince Ras Mekonen, and the current building was constructed by Emperor Haile Selassie to accommodate the growing number of faithful who travel from across Ethiopia to celebrate the feast.
stGabriel.p3: Saint Gabriel is remembered for his miraculous works, including the saving of the three children — Anania, Azaria, and Misael — from the burning fire, as told in the Book of Daniel, Chapter 3.

dates.name: Hamle 19 (July 26)
dates.description: Commemorates the day the Ark of Saint Gabriel entered the temple at Kulubi

dates.name: Tahsas 19 (December 28)
dates.description: Celebrates the consecration of Kulubi Saint Gabriel Church and the miraculous saving of the three children from the fire

stGabriel.monthly: The 19th of every Ethiopian month is also observed as a day of Saint Gabriel.

sundaySchool.title: Sunday School
sundaySchool.p: Our Sunday School (Yesunday Timhirt Bet) provides children and young people with religious education, Amharic language classes, and Ge'ez hymn learning. Classes run alongside Saturday morning services.
